tx_south_rim_wall.blurb: South Rim Wall is the biggest cliff at Camp Eagle, a riverside property in the Texas hill country near Rocksprings. It holds a dozen climbs: eleven bolted sport routes and a single boulder problem on limestone. The grades start around 5.7 and run up through the 5.10s and 5.11s into a couple of 5.12 lines, so there is something for a mid-grade leader and a few projects for stronger climbers. The setting is scenic and airy, with a lot of drop to the river below. The wall is reached from the neighbouring Main Wall along a high ledge, so expect a little exposure before you ever tie in. Quiet, with few other sport climbers around.

tx_power_of_silence_area.blurb: A small bouldering pocket on North Mountain at Hueco Tanks, east of El Paso, set in a narrow corridor. Eleven problems are recorded, and most are on the easy side: a cluster of V2s, with Gums the busiest line, plus a V1. The upper end is steep in difficulty, with a V5 and V6 and then a handful of serious problems from V9 to V11, including the namesake line. Pads and spotters are a good idea here because the corridor is tight. It makes a handy stop for a mixed group, giving warm-up problems and a few hard projects within a short stroll of each other.

tx_martini_roof_area.blurb: Martini Roof is a compact, hard-leaning bouldering zone on North Mountain at Hueco Tanks, outside El Paso. Eleven problems are recorded, built around a big chalked roof that marks the spot. This is not a beginner stop: the easiest problem is around V5, most sit between V6 and V9, and the top end reaches V12 and beyond, up into the very hardest tier of the park. The roof keeps the lines steep and sheltered, and the spot is described as shady and able to stay dry in wet weather. It can draw a crowd, so be ready to share the landing.

tx_serpent_wall.blurb: Serpent Wall is a short limestone wall at Reimers Ranch, west of Austin, standing a little way along from the busier Dead Cats Wall and just around the corner from Zoey's Wall. About 25 feet tall with a roof near the base, it has eleven climbs, almost all bolted sport routes plus one top-rope variation. The bulk of the routes fall at 5.8 and 5.9, with one easier line, a single 5.10 and two 5.11s to stretch toward. The wall is semi-shady and can fill up at busy times, but its modest height makes for quick laps.

tx_guide_s_wall.blurb: Guide's Wall is a short limestone crag in the Gus Fruh section of the Barton Creek Greenbelt in Austin, the farthest right of the walls there. The eleven climbs run roughly 30 feet, mostly bolted sport lines with a few top-rope setups and one trad route. Grades go from 5.6 up to 5.10, with about half the routes around 5.10 and the rest easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. That mix has long made it a favourite for lessons and for climbers taking their first leads. Pockets, crimps and bulgy moves are the style. Weekend afternoons see classes and groups, so early starts are quieter.
tx_guide_s_wall.parking_note: Leave the car on the street near the Barton Creek Greenbelt trail sign. From South Lamar, turn onto Barton Skyway and continue to the second four-way stop, then go left.
tx_guide_s_wall.approach: From the trail sign, follow the path down to the creek and wade across, then turn right and go along the bank for about 150 yards. A wall with a cave at its base comes first; Guide's Wall is the next one on the left.

tx_zoey_s_wall.blurb: Zoey's Wall is a small, easy-going crag at Reimers Ranch, west of Austin, beside the main trail that leads in to the bigger walls. Its ten or so climbs are mostly short bolted sport routes, with one top-rope line and a single trad route, and the grades stay low: a few beginner-level climbs, then a cluster from 5.6 to 5.9. Routes are only about 20 feet tall, so it is not a destination for mileage, but it works well for introducing someone to climbing or for a first lead. Zoey's Arete, a mellow 5.5, is the best-known line. Serpent Wall is just around the corner.
